Package com.jasonwjones.pbcs.client.impl

Class PbcsExplicitDimensionsPlanTypeImpl

java.lang.Object
com.jasonwjones.pbcs.client.impl.AbstractPbcsObject
com.jasonwjones.pbcs.client.impl.PbcsPlanTypeImpl
com.jasonwjones.pbcs.client.impl.PbcsExplicitDimensionsPlanTypeImpl
All Implemented Interfaces:
PbcsExplicitDimensionsPlanType, PbcsObject, PbcsPlanType
public class PbcsExplicitDimensionsPlanTypeImpl extends PbcsPlanTypeImpl implements PbcsExplicitDimensionsPlanType
A plan type implementation where the known dimensions are explicitly defined. Defining the list of explicit dimensions is usually handled by having an additional property on the connection settings. For example, an additional query parameter can be appended to your cube/plan name, such as Basic?dimensions=Period;Years;Scenario.

Hopefully someday the process of getting the dimensions for a plan will be better supported by the EPM Cloud REST API but for now this lets us significantly enrich functionality.

  • Method Details

    • getDimensions

      public List<PbcsDimension> getDimensions()
      Description copied from interface: PbcsPlanType
      Gets the list of dimensions for this plan/cube. This will be either the explicitly specified dimensions for this cube (if defined), otherwise a call is made to the unofficial data management (DM) endpoint that provides dimensional information. In the past, I've seen issues with permissions where low-level users couldn't access this endpoint, so be careful how you architect your solutions with this.

      Additionally, in the past I've also seen issues where the cube may have not been synced properly and the list of dimensions was bogus. I don't know if this was a timing/configuration thing or some other issue where the DM dimensions were out of sync.

      Specified by:

    • getMemberOrAlias

      public PbcsMember getMemberOrAlias(String memberOrAliasName)
      Description copied from interface: PbcsPlanType
      Similar to PbcsPlanType.getMember(String), this is provided as a convenience to try and find a member using its name or alias. The implementation for this method is a little different compared to its counterpart. This method will perform a brute-force search through the explicit dimensions, fetch the root member, and then traverse the hierarchy looking for any member with a matching name or alias. The comparison is performed in a case-insensitive manner.

      As with the other convenience method, this search process is potentially expensive in that it's possible every dimension needs to be searched to find the member. Further, this method does not currently participate in the member to dimension cache process, so if you plan on hitting this method a lot (such as to resolve names across a large data grid) you will almost certainly want to use a cache, such as exists in CachingPbcsPlanType (not currently part of this library).

      Specified by:
      getMemberOrAlias in interface PbcsPlanType
      Overrides:
      getMemberOrAlias in class PbcsPlanTypeImpl
      Parameters:
      memberOrAliasName - the member name or alias to search for
      Returns:
      the member for the given name or alias, or null if none is found across all the known dimensions

    • retrieve

      public DataSliceGrid retrieve()
      Description copied from interface: PbcsPlanType
      Perform a "default" retrieve against this plan/cube. This only works when the dimensions have been specified using explicit dimensions (e.g., using PbcsApplication.getPlanType(PbcsApplication.PlanTypeConfiguration)) where the configuration has a list of dimensions provided. Internally, the retrieve is performed using the standard "export data slice" REST endpoint; the dimension list is needed to fill out a grid with one cell using a member from each dimension. This method is essentially offered for convenience and "smoke testing".
      Specified by:
      retrieve in interface PbcsPlanType
      Overrides:
      retrieve in class PbcsPlanTypeImpl
      Returns:
      a data slice for a default retrieve from the cube
